heard: The moon's first rover was built to last three days. Instead, it survived 11 lunar days and drove six miles. A radioactive polonium core kept it warm through freezing nights. Contact went dark in 1971, leaving it lost for decades. An orbiter spotted the rover sitting in the dust in 2010. Scientists fired a telescope blazer at its French mirror. On the first try, it bounced back 2,000 photons. It outshined newer lunar reflectors, proving how it broke every record.
